title: Slice curation and human review playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose / scope:
This doc is a working playbook for curating traffic slices for LLM canaries and integrating human review checkpoints (HITL) during progressive exposure. Focus: practical heuristics for picking slices, a lightweight annotation pipeline for safety/quality signals, and operational rules to keep canaries small and reversible.

Audience:
- Product release owners
- Experiment owners
- SRE/Observability
- Solutions / CS for customer-sensitive slices

Non-goals:
- Full statistical power calculations (separate stat-tech doc)
- End-to-end automation; aim for semi-automated operator flows first

1) Slice curation checklist (one-pager)
- Define hypothesis: what behavior are we testing? (e.g., safety regression for policy X, reranker recall, latency-sensitive prompt patterns)
- Impact axis: customer-facing vs internal; map each slice to impact bucket (low/medium/high)
- Cardinality estimate: expected QPS and unique users per slice (use last 30d sample)
- Feasibility: can we identify slice reliably in routing layer? (yes/partial/no)
- Human-review need: yes if high-impact or ambiguous outputs
- Rollout cadence suggestion: tiny (0.1%-1%), small (1-5%), medium (5-20%)

2) Sampling matrix (quick refer)
- Deterministic slices: account type, region, endpoint route -> prefer larger sample sizes
- Model-behavior slices: prompt-template clusters, instruction-following -> prefer stratified sampling + priority hitl
- Rare-event slices: profanity, legal-phrasing, hallucination-prone queries -> synthetic upsampling + mandatory human review

3) Human review pipeline (lightweight)
- Trigger rules:
  - Fallbacks: when model confidence below threshold OR reranker score drop > 30%
  - Safety signals: token-level policy flags OR regex matches for sensitive keywords
  - Performance signals: latency > SLO or truncated generation occurrences
- Queue architecture:
  - Tier 1: triage reviewers (internal ops) — cursory pass, bin into accept/reject/escalate
  - Tier 2: subject-matter reviewers (legal/CS) — deep review for escalated content
- SLA targets: Tier1 < 15m median; Tier2 < 4h for high-impact slices
- Sampling budget: start with 200 labeled outputs/day per critical slice, adjust after week 1

4) Annotation guide (short)
- Label fields: acceptability (Y/N), severity (low/med/high), hallucination (Y/N), PII leakage (Y/N), notes
- Example labels with snippet guidelines (3-5 examples)
- Inter-annotator goal: 0.7 Cohen's kappa minimum for new slice profiles

5) Metrics & alerts to surface in console
- Slice-level SLA: p95 latency, token cost per request, error rate
- Quality signals: percent rejected by human review; per-slice BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-similarity to reference when available
- Safety signals: policy flags per 1k requests, PII-touch rate
- Escalation thresholds (auto page): >5% reject rate for 24h on high-impact slice; safety flags >10 per hour

6) Rollout gating rules
- Gate A (smoke): internal-only traffic, automated checks pass for 24h, reject rate <2%
- Gate B (limited external): 1% traffic, hitl sample running, SLA metrics meet targets for 48h
- Gate C (expanded): 10% traffic, canary monitors green for 72h and no customer escalations
- Reversion criteria: any gate breach OR manual veto from oncall/product owner

7) Operational playbook (ops checklist)
- Pre-activation: update runbook, notify SRE & CS, ensure observability dashboards exist
- Activation: run smoke tests (synthetic and live), enable metric collectors, start hitl sampling
- Mid-run: daily check-ins first 3 days, then cadence to weekly when stable
- Post-run: capture learnings and map to model/quantization changes; compute cost delta

8) Simulation plan (quick experiments before live)
- Shadow traffic: route copy of 5-10% to canary model, compare outputs against control with diffs & policy flags
- Synthetic stress: generate 1k worst-case prompts (from historical tail) and run through pipeline
- Human-in-loop dry run: run annotation pipeline on historical outputs to validate labeling throughput and kappa

9) Roles & responsibilities
- Experiment owner: defines hypothesis, slice, acceptance criteria
- Traffic steward (product/ops): curates routing and sample weights
- Observability engineer: dashboards, alerts, instrumentation hooks
- SRE oncall: capacity & rollback ability
- CS/Legal reviewer: subject-matter escalation

10) Cost & capacity considerations
- Human review cost estimate: assume 2 minutes per review at Tier1, 10min per Tier2 -> compute FTE based on sample budget
- Model execution cost: shadowing and synthetic runs increase token cost; cap shadow QPS to avoid capacity impact

Open questions / TODOs:
- Automating slice extraction from embeddings stream (Leah/Ops to prototype)
- Stat method: exact sample size per-slice to reach 90% power (link to stat-tech doc)
- How to synthesize rare safety cases without creating recall bias?
- Integrate with rollout orchestration API (PR #401) to make hitl toggles first-class

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Example query to estimate slice cardinality (psql):
  SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE route='search-v2' AND country='BR' AND date > now() - interval '30 days';
- Sample pseudo-routing rule (yaml):
  - name: "hitl-low-confidence"
    match: "model_confidence < 0.6 && route == 'compose'"
    action: "route_to_hitl_queue"

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and operator-focused; please add concrete counters or missing alert thresholds you rely on during canaries.
- If you own a customer-specific slice, add a short example under the "slice examples" section with identifiers we can use to route traffic.
